extracted.intended_audience: IB Mathematics Standard Level students preparing their Internal Assessment (IA) / summer assignment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation rubric for producing the IB Math SL Internal Assessment (exploration) rough draft and final paper, including required structure, mathematical presentation, personal engagement, reflection, and submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and emphasis on precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Final paper: 6–12 pages. Rough draft: at least 900 words. No specific word count due to inclusion of computations, graphs, diagrams, tables, etc. In a math paper, precision, logic and clarity count more than length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More work done on the draft now reduces work later. Do not equate longer with better; avoid repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper copy of the draft is due on the first day of class and the draft must also be submitted via Blackboard SafeAssign. Submit as a Word document or an editable PDF; do NOT use Google Docs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Google Docs — you will lose computations, formatting and equations. You will receive feedback in the fall; submit editable formats so edits are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction must state your rationale (purpose for choosing the topic) as well as your thesis statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a clear aim for the exploration. To meet IB standards the exploration must contain an introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration content requirements (required components)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exploration must be a logically developed exploration easy to follow by peers and MUST include: citing references (use MLA), stating appropriate definitions and explanations of concepts, use of precise notation, applicable graphs and mathematical computations, and personal engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite references, direct quotes, etc., in MLA format. Use appropriate mathematical notation and symbols; include graphs/tables/diagrams at appropriate places (not simply tacked on at the end). Define key terms where required. Ensure representations enhance reader understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal engagement (Criterion C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exploration is assessed for evidence of personal engagement (levels 0–4 from limited to outstanding). Personal engagement is the student's independent/creative thinking, addressing personal interest, or presenting mathematical ideas in their own way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: creating your own code, learning and describing unfamiliar math topics, collecting original data (e.g., runners' times) and analyzing it exhaustively using learned techniques. Personal engagement includes asking questions, making conjectures, choosing topics of genuine interest, and applying mathematics to real-world situations or historical/global perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion and reflection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusion should tie up major ideas, answer 'So what?', discuss how reasonable results and conclusions appear, consider ramifications and usefulness, suggest further study, note what went wrong and why, and connect to TOK where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities for reflection lie mostly in the conclusion but can appear throughout. Discuss implications, significance, limitations/extensions, and links to other fields or areas of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer assignment checklist (submission checklist scored out of 40)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rubric of four checklist items used for the rough draft (each worth 10 points): (1) Did the student submit the rough draft on time? (2) Was the rough draft at least 900 words? (3) Was the draft coherent (had an aim/rationale, showed development, or at least stated where it was going)? (4) Did the rough draft use appropriate mathematical terminology and vocabulary (no calculator notation, use proper terms)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total = 40 points. Example anti-patterns: using calculator notation (^, *, etc.), using casual words like 'plug in' instead of 'substitute'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion A – Communication (IB rubric, achievement levels 0–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses identification of a clear aim and the communication of ideas: coherence, organization, concision and completeness. Levels range from 'does not reach standard' to 'coherent, well-organized, concise and complete'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bullets from IB: identify a clear aim; express ideas clearly; focus on the aim and avoid irrelevance; structure ideas logically; include graphs, tables and diagrams at appropriate places (not appended separately); cite references. To score above a 2 the exploration must contain an introduction, a logically organized explanation, and a conclusion. Define terms unfamiliar to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion B – Mathematical presentation (IB rubric, achievement levels 0–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses appropriate mathematical language and representation (notation, symbols, terminology) and the use of multiple forms of representation (tables, graphs, formulas, diagrams, charts, models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT use calculator notation or include calculator keystrokes. Do NOT describe how to use Excel or other software. Define key terms where required. Express results to an appropriate degree of accuracy (3 significant figures). When writing an approximation use '≈' not '='. Minor inconsistent errors are acceptable; consistent errors (e.g., using '=' for approximations) will prevent marks above the lower levels. Avoid casual words like 'plug in' and 'tweak' — use 'substitute' and 'modify'. Include only representations that enhance understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion D – Reflection (IB rubric, achievement levels 0–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the depth of reflection in the exploration from limited/superficial to substantial/critical. Reflection considers implications, the significance of results, limitations and possible extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conclusion and moments in your writing to reflect: e.g., if using statistics, discuss whether selected techniques could slant data presentation and the impacts on stakeholders. Consider limitations of models and possible extensions (e.g., a fish migration model: can it model birds or people?). Make links to other fields/areas of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion E – Use of mathematics (IB rubric, achievement levels 0–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether relevant mathematics commensurate with the course level is used and how correctly it is applied; levels describe increasing correctness and understanding from 'some relevant mathematics' to 'mathematics explored is correct with thorough knowledge and understanding'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose mathematics at an appropriate level (neither too elementary nor beyond your current knowledge). Minor errors are acceptable but consistent errors will limit the mark to low levels. Demonstrate application of mathematics to different contexts and problem-solving techniques, and recognize/explain patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and vocabulary rules (style and anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit stylistic/notation rules emphasized across the rubric: use precise mathematical notation and appropriate terminology; avoid calculator notation and keystrokes; use correct symbols for approximations; avoid informal verbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules: do not use calculator notation such as '^' or '*'; do not include calculator keystrokes; express approximations to 3 significant figures where appropriate and write approximations with '≈'; avoid casual wording: use 'substitute' (not 'plug in') and 'modify' (not 'tweak'); do not include charts/diagrams merely to fill space; place graphs/tables inline where they are discussed rather than solely in an appendix.
